_comment: WP-54 Diktálás: what Voice/fetch.js downloads into <Full>/tools/voice. The engine is pinned to a release TAG; every file is checked against its sha256. A null sha256 is filled in once by `node Voice/fetch.js --pin <id>` after you have checked the download (the first fetch on H:, 2026-11); commit the manifest afterwards. Nothing here goes into the repo except this file.

engine.note: CPU build for Windows x64. A GPU build (cuBLAS / Vulkan) can replace it later; the adapter does not change.

models.note: The best Hungarian of the fast models; 4 decoder layers, so re-decoding the growing buffer stays quick on a modern CPU.
The fallback for a slow machine: much quicker partials, clearly weaker Hungarian.
Only to compare: slower than turbo (24 decoder layers), Hungarian not better.

ocr._comment: WP-56 Szem: the OCR fallback of the screen reader. tessdata_fast pinned to the 4.1.0 TAG, fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com (github.com/…/raw is refused by some proxies) by `node Voice/screen/fetch-ocr.js` into <Full>/tools/voice/tessdata, every file checked against its sha256 (measured 2026-11-25). The engine itself is tesseract.js 7.0.0 from npm, pinned with sha512 integrity in Voice/screen/package-lock.json.

tts._comment: WP-57 Hang: what Voice/tts/fetch-tts.js downloads into <Full>/tools/voice/tts. npm packages are pinned to an exact version and checked against their sha512 integrity (the repo's npm rule); voice archives are pinned to the sherpa-onnx `tts-models` release and checked against sha256. Stay on sherpa-onnx-node 1.13.x: 2.0.0 dropped the built-in espeak-ng phonemizer, so Piper voices fail there ('phoneme_codepoints is empty').

addon.name: sherpa-onnx-node
addon.note: Prebuilt N-API addon (no compiler needed). Released 2026-09-10.

voices.license: UNCLEAR: dataset CC0 (NabuCasa voice-datasets), but fine-tuned from Piper en_US lessac (Blizzard 2013 data); check before any use outside the Founder's own PC
UNCLEAR: model card says 'See URL' (MycroftAI mimic3-voices); fine-tuned from lessac

identity._comment: WP-59 Hangazonosítás: what Voice/identity/fetch-identity.js downloads into <Full>/tools/voice/identity. Speaker-embedding models from sherpa-onnx's GitHub release `speaker-recongition-models` (the upstream spelling), checked against sha256. They run on the SAME sherpa-onnx-node 1.13.8 addon as Voice/tts (fetch it with `node Voice/tts/fetch-tts.js addon`). Scores below were measured in the cloud on synthetic Piper voices (plumbing only, not real-world accuracy); calibrate on the owner's own voice with Voice/identity/calibrate.js.

models.eer: 0.73 % EER on VoxCeleb1-O (3D-Speaker egs/voxceleb/sv-cam++ README; 0.65 % with large-margin fine-tuning)
models.note: Best separation of the three on synthetic voices here (owner 0.72–0.90, others ≤ 0.42) and the fastest (≈ 38 ms a verify on 2 cores; ≈ 0.34 s to load).

models.eer: ResNet34 ≈ 0.7–1.0 % on VoxCeleb1-O (WeSpeaker / 3D-Speaker tables; not re-checked for this exact export)
models.license: WeSpeaker code Apache-2.0; its VoxCeleb models follow the dataset licence, CC BY 4.0 (wespeaker docs/pretrained.md)
models.note: Narrower gap on synthetic voices (others up to 0.69): an alternative, not the default.
